statedReasoning: This is a Senate bill (senátní návrh, submitted by Senate President Miloš Vystrčil on behalf of the Senate, sponsor listed in the brief as 'Aschenbrenner L. a další') amending § 32 of zákon č. 256/2004 Sb., o podnikání na kapitálovém trhu (Capital Markets Business Act, 'ZPKT'). Having now read the full bill text and důvodová zpráva, the substance is a narrow, technical scope-narrowing amendment concerning investiční zprostředkovatelé (investment intermediaries, 'IZ') -- a category of small, self-employed-agent-like intermediaries who are expressly excluded from Directive 2014/65/EU (MiFID II). The bill replaces the word 'obdobně' ('equivalently/analogously') with 'přiměřeně' ('proportionately') throughout § 32, and adds a new §32(7) stating that EU Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/565 (the MiFID II organizational/operational delegated act) applies to IZ only 'proportionately' via this explicit statutory reference -- not automatically as the Czech National Bank (ČNB) had been applying it through what the DZ calls an unsupported 'abstract implementing relationship' (abstraktní prováděcí vztah). The stated purpose (DZ parts 1-3) is to correct ČNB's allegedly over-broad interpretive practice that imposed MiFID-II-grade regulatory burden, designed for large investment firms (obchodníci s cennými papíry, OCP), onto small investment intermediaries who are legally exempt from MiFID II's own scope -- i.e. a deregulatory correction aligning IZ obligations back down to MiFID II's actual minimum requirement under Art. 3 MiFID II. The bill's own corruption-risk section states a formal CIA (Corrupt Impact Assessment) was performed and found the change creates no new corruption risk. Effective date proposed: 1 Jan 2027. Signed by Senate President Miloš Vystrčil, 6 Mar 2026.
researchedContext: The census confirms the graph's recorded amended law (256/2004 Sb.) matches the real amended law exactly -- amendedLawsRealFromCensus shows realLaws=[256/2004], recordedLaws=[256/2004], undercount=0, consistent with this being a single-subject, single-paragraph (§32) bill rather than an omnibus. Legislative history independently confirms: Senate submission 9 Mar 2026, distribution to the Chamber as tisk 132/0 on 11 Mar 2026, a negative government position (nesouhlas) returned 1 Apr 2026 (tisk 132/1), and Organizational Committee proceeding recommendation on 2 Apr 2026 with Ing. Libor Turek, Ph.D. as rapporteur and the Budget Committee as guarantor. The bill's substantive effect -- narrowing ČNB's application of an EU delegated regulation to a specific, small class of market intermediaries -- is a deregulatory move for that class, but it is the EXPLICITLY STATED purpose of the bill (not a hidden or unstated effect), so it is reported here as statedReasoning rather than as an unstatedEffects entry.
